cells.tense: You're still at it after everything, and today that steadiness is just where you live.
cells.ask: Offer one practice or story from your own keeping to somebody newer, and let them keep it — that's the strength staying in circulation.
cells.core:
A kitchen where the old recipe is being taught and the room is full of somebody else's hands doing it, badly, and you're fine with that. The practice passes to the next person and keeps working in their hands, changed a little, still itself. You keep things going without clamping down on them, and the holding doesn't cost you what it holds. You can hold something up without gripping it.

Pick one thing from your own keeping and pass it to somebody newer, with no plan for what they do with it. Your own tried strength gets somewhere new to go.
cells.sheetLine: You keep it going without clamping it down.
cells.verb: keep on with what you're still hoping for
cells.place: in what gets handed down and shared between people

cells.tense: You're braced against what's coming for the tradition, spending the strength you have on a fight that hasn't arrived.
cells.ask: Weigh what's actually in front of you once before answering for how it'll go — the knowing holds fine undecided for a day.
cells.core:
A table where the people who use the practice are the ones who shape it, and you listen before you add your own piece. The shared thing gets checked against the room before it goes out, and that's the work going right. Lately you're defending it from a threat that hasn't shown up. Every gathering, every handoff, every small wording gets a prepared case against how it'll land.

The defending is what's wearing the thing down. Weigh what's actually in front of you before you answer for how it will go — some things hold better left undecided for a day.

cells.tense: There's something in the shared keeping you can't pick up again, and it's been sitting behind you for a while.
cells.ask: Tend one small piece of the shared thing this week — a meal, a letter, a standing date — enough to know it still grows from care.
cells.core:
The table that's set for you because you always showed up, and the language you never had to reach for because it was just there. Keeping something going is second nature when nothing strains it, tending what's already under your hands, and the practice stays alive because the tending happens.

What's here now is the held part gone quiet. Gatherings keep happening and you're not in them. The fact you can still draw on a proved strength is not in question; what's missing is showing up again. Tend one small piece of what's shared this week, gently, without needing it to amount to much, and let that be enough for now.
cells.sheetLine: You've stopped picking up what you still know how to hold.
cells.verb: keep on with what you're still hoping for
cells.place: in what gets handed down and shared between people

cells.tense: You're carrying more for the shared thing than you'll say, and it's getting described as the thing carrying itself.
cells.ask: Say out loud that one piece of the shared tradition is yours to hold — as a fact, to yourself or anyone — and keep holding it just as it is.
cells.core:
The practice running clean because somebody's been tending it without a fuss, and the people who receive it never see the hands behind the work. The steady handing-on you do is why it still reaches anybody, and it feels most like itself when nobody has to name who's behind it.

Right now it goes on because you keep it going, and nobody, including you, is calling it yours. It's still being carried. The carrying just hasn't been claimed. Say once, plainly, that holding this piece of it is yours — you're allowed to name it without asking anything of it — and let that be true before anything changes.
cells.sheetLine: You keep it going and call it nobody's doing.
